text: In November of 2013, thirty-three of us said "employment non-discrimination act," peaking together on the seventh; thirty-two of us said "the employment non-discrimination act" that same day. Twenty-four of us reached for "non-discrimination act enda," twenty-three for "employment non-discrimination act enda," and twenty-two for "the employment non-discrimination act enda," all cresting on November seventh. Twenty-one of us said "sexual orientation or gender," nineteen the fuller "sexual orientation or gender identity." Eighteen of us said "discrimination based on." The first among us to say "employment non-discrimination act" did so on February twentieth; the enda formulations we date to April twenty-fifth. We converged on a single day. We record that our language moved as one that November, and we leave the record as it stands.
